paper_title: ASyMOB Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
caption: belowskip=0pt : Effect of equivalence-type perturbations. Note the substantial drop in success rate for most models, even when performance on the seed set is high.

model_annotations.English: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the success rate of various artificial intelligence models across different equivalence-type perturbations. The horizontal axis contains the categories, consisting of specific model names and conditions (such as "Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)", "DeepSeek-R1", and "GPT-4o") presented with rotated text labels; these categories do not appear to be sorted alphabetically or strictly by value. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "Success Rate (%)", and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100 with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 20. For each model category on the horizontal axis, the chart displays a grouped set of five adjacent vertical bars. According to the top-right legend, these bars represent different test conditions coded by varying shades of blue: the darkest blue represents the "Seed" condition, followed by progressively lighter shades for "'Equivalence-One-Easy'", "'Equivalence-One-Hard'", "'Equivalence-All-Easy'", and finally the lightest blue for "'Equivalence-All-Hard'". Visually, there is a consistent trend within almost every group where the bar height progressively decreases from the darkest blue "Seed" bar on the left to the lightest blue "'Equivalence-All-Hard'" bar on the right. The tallest bars in the chart are the "Seed" bars for "Gemini 2.5 Flash (No Code)" and "o4-mini (Code)", both approaching approximately 98% to 100%. The shortest bars approach 0%, predominantly occurring in the "'Equivalence-All-Hard'" condition for models such as "Gemma 3 27B", "GPT-4o", and "GPT-4o mini". The chart does not utilize any specific visual emphasis, such as bolding or outlines, for individual bars.
model_annotations.German: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the effect of different equivalence-type perturbations on the success rate of various language models. The horizontal category axis displays 17 distinct model configurations, with labels rotated diagonally, including models such as Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code), o4-mini (Code), DeepSeek-R1, and GPT-4o, arranged categorically rather than in strict alphabetical or descending order. The vertical value axis is labeled "Success Rate (%)" and features a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with numeric tick marks spaced at intervals of 20 units. Data is organized into clustered groups of five bars for each model category on the horizontal axis. A legend in the top right corner defines the five components within each group using a gradient of blue hues: the darkest blue represents the "Seed" condition, followed by medium-dark blue for "'Equivalence-One-Easy'", medium blue for "'Equivalence-One-Hard'", light blue for "'Equivalence-All-Easy'", and the lightest blue for "'Equivalence-All-Hard'". Within each group, the bars are arranged side-by-side in this order from left to right. Visually, the bars exhibit a consistent pattern across the model groups, where the "Seed" bar is typically the tallest and the subsequent bars progressively decrease in height, making the "'Equivalence-All-Hard'" bar the shortest in almost every cluster. The highest overall values in the chart are found in the "Seed" category, with the tallest bars reaching approximately 98% to 99% for the Gemini 2.5 Flash (No Code) and o4-mini (Code) models. Conversely, the shortest bars belong to the "'Equivalence-All-Hard'" category for several models on the right side of the axis, such as Gemma 3 27B and GPT-4o mini, measuring at approximately 1% to 3%. The chart does not utilize any specific visual emphasis techniques such as bolding, additional shading, or outlining for individual bars.
